title: How Josh Allen, Bills overcame disastrous 5-turnover day to hand Chargers' third loss
description: Buffalo's ball security was lackluster in Week 3, but the Bills still managed to escape the Chargers at home.
fullText:
How Josh Allen, Bills overcame disastrous 5-turnover day to hand Chargers' third loss originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

To get to 3-0, the Bills had to win ugly.

In the second game they've played at the new Highmark Stadium, Buffalo remained unbeaten while keeping the Chargers winless with a 17-13 victory on Sunday afternoon. Yet, compared to their first two games, it was a disastrous performance by the Bills' offense.

Buffalo had a total of five turnovers in Sunday's game, but thanks to a pair of Josh Allen tush-push touchdowns and opportunistic plays defensively, the Bills escaped with a win.

Here's a look at how Buffalo overcame a sloppy day to stay undefeated.

MORE:Drake Maye's turnover issues continue with ugly showing vs. Jaguars

The Bills had five giveaways in Week 3 to the Chargers' one. According to Nick Suss, the last time Buffalo won a game with a minus-four turnover differential or worse was on Sept. 21, 1997, against the Colts — a day that Jim Harbaugh was Indianapolis' starting quarterback.

This time, with Harbaugh on the sidelines, the Chargers appeared to find some needed momentum early. On the Bills' first play from scrimmage, James Cook fumbled the ball away.

CHARGERS HAVE THE FOOTBALL AFTER THE BILLS FUMBLE

📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/ibsrq8adUI

A few drives later, Josh Allen's pass was picked off by Genesis Smith, a rough start for Buffalo.

Genesis Smith picks it off and the Chargers have forced two turnovers in the first quarter@LACvsBUF on FOX/FOX One
Stream on @NFLPluspic.twitter.com/ZPNmigdnpQ

On the first play of the second quarter, with the Bills still scoreless, Smith got Allen again.

Genesis Smith with a crazy INT! His second of the day!@LACvsBUF on FOX/FOX One
Stream on @NFLPluspic.twitter.com/V0MvvChSyb

Buffalo finally got its offense going to pull within three by the second half, but a big hit to Dalton Kincaid knocked the ball free for a fumble recovered by the Chargers in the third quarter.

CHARGERS FORCE ANOTHER BILLS TURNOVER 🤯

📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/jnBggGooYA

Finally, on the first play of the fourth quarter, a review reversed a call on an Allen sack, with a Khalil Mack takedown resulting in a fumble — Allen's third turnover.

JOSH ALLEN FUMBLED THE BALL

WHAT A CHALLENGE pic.twitter.com/zybZY5k4u8

The story of the Chargers' loss was their missed opportunities. Despite the five Bills turnovers and another 10 penalties for Buffalo, Los Angeles continually couldn't take advantage, with Justin Herbert throwing an interception himself and the Chargers settling for field goals.

CJ Gardner-Johnson intercepts it and takes it back near midfield @LACvsBUF on FOX/FOX One
Stream on @NFLPluspic.twitter.com/9Aro5CR7G7

After Allen's third turnover of the day, Herbert threw his interception, which led to a Buffalo touchdown drive. Over 13 plays and a grind of penalty issues, Allen finally snuck one into the end zone to give his team the late lead.

Another Josh Allen sneak for a TD and the Bills take the lead!@LACvsBUF on FOX/FOX One
Stream on @NFLPluspic.twitter.com/8xTA89EPx8

Harbaugh allowed the Chargers to go for a 4th & 10 on the following drive, which resulted in a turnover on downs — and James Cook led the way to break the game open for Buffalo.

James Cook is in! Bills make it a two-score game late@LACvsBUF on FOX/FOX One
Stream on @NFLPluspic.twitter.com/4BF0DLmnXK

The Bills put all of their miscues to rest as Cook's touchdown made it a two-score game, essentially putting the Chargers away for their third loss of the season.

title: Instant analysis of Colts' Week 3 win over Texans
description: Here are our instant takeaways from Indianapolis Colts' performance against Houston in Week 3.
fullText:
The Indianapolis Colts avoided a nearly devastating loss to the Houston Texans, retaking the lead late on a Spencer Shrader field goal.

With the win, the Colts improved to 1-2 on the season. Here are our instant takeaways from Indianapolis' performance against Houston.

- The Colts' nine-game losing streak dating back to last season has now ended. Although it's only Week 3, this was a playoff-like game for Indianapolis, with history not kind to 0-3 teams when it comes to making the playoffs.

- It was certainly a better performance from the Colts' defense in this game. CJ Stroud passed for only 169 yards, while the Texans averaged under 4.0 yards per carry on the ground. With the Indianapolis offense turning the ball over three times, the defense was put in some difficult situations but often held up.

- Against a disruptive Houston defense, things didn't come easily for the Colts' offense either. The run game averaged just 2.9 YPC, while Daniel Jones averaged a modest 6.5 yards per pass attempt on 36 passes.

- This was not Jones' sharpest performance, by any means.

- Jones did face pressure in this game, with Will Anderson often in the backfield. Jones and the pass game did create some chunk plays in those situations, but Jones also made a bad decision on the interception he threw, and he put the ball on the ground multiple times as well.

- Jones and the passing game found some success over the middle of the field.

- We know that Josh Downs is a reliable target, but he's showcased his ability to generate some chunk plays over the last two weeks without Alec Pierce.

- Tyler Warren continues to be targeted heavily, however, it's often around the line of scrimmage, where defenders are quick to swarm. He averaged just 6.1 yards per reception. Shane Steichen has to find different ways to get him the ball.

- Despite the inconsistent play at times from the Colts' offense, this unit was relatively efficient on third downs, which helped extend drives. That allowed the Colts to also control the time of possession and limit Houston's opportunities on offense.

- While not perfect, the Colts' pass rush did seem more disruptive today than it had been during the first two games.

- The secondary was also able to limit explosive pass plays, which is something that was a big issue through the first two weeks.

- Spencer Shrader showcased why he won the kicking competition over the summer. A terrific outing for him as he dealt with a groin injury.

- A disruptive day for Adetomiwa Adebawore along the Colts' interior defensive line. Also a bounce-back performance from Justin Walley.

This article originally appeared on Colts Wire: Instant analysis of Colts' Week 3 win over Texans

title: Patrick Mahomes, Chiefs benefit from ref’s questionable roughing penalty vs Dolphins
description: The Chiefs used a bad penalty to turn a punt into a field goal.
fullText:
How do you know the Kansas City Chiefs are really back? Fans are convinced that referees are making bad calls that go in their favor. That's exactly what happened during the Chiefs Week 3 game against the Miami Dolphins. Patrick Mahomes got hit hard while throwing a pass and flags immediately started flying.

Facing third-and-nine in the third quarter, Mahomes dropped back to pass in the end zone. Just as he was throwing the ball to Rashee Rice he was hit by Chop Robinson. Robinson didn't hit Mahomes in the head or neck. He made first contact while the ball was still in Mahomes' hand. It was a hard hit, but it was clean.

They decided Robinson was guilty of landing on Mahomes with all his bodyweight, but where exactly was he supposed to go?

MORE: Cris Collinsworth admits to his deep love for Chiefs' Patrick Mahomes

In what world is this roughing the passer? Does not hit to the head or neck area, and makes the best attempt to not land on him with his full body weight. 

Mahomes and the Chiefs draw the penalty… pic.twitter.com/xvkAG2Irh3

— Rate the Refs (@Rate_the_Refs) September 27, 2026

If they hadn't made this call, the Chiefs would have punted. Instead, they took the fresh set of downs and marched down the field to kick a field goal and extend their lead to 17-10.

MORE: Indiana Fever's Sophie Cunningham compares herself to Patrick Mahomes

The Chiefs went on to win the game 24-10 and are now 3-0. Mahomes completed 20-of-24 passes for 246 yards and two touchdown passes. One of those touchdowns went to Travis Kelce. His second of the season. Kenneth Walker III had a quiet 18 carries for 70 yards.

The Chiefs will travel to Las Vegas next week to take on the Raiders. Don't worry, the refs will be there too.

title: Orioles-Yankees regular-season finale canceled because of rain
description: The regular-season finale between the Baltimore Orioles and New York Yankees on Sunday was canceled because of sustained rain.  New York will host Boston in an AL Wild Card Series starting Tuesday.  Cam Schlittler will start Game 1 on Tuesday, followed by Max Fried and Gerrit Cole.
fullText:
NEW YORK (AP) — The regular-season finale between the Baltimore Orioles and New York Yankees on Sunday was canceled because of sustained rain.

New York will host Boston in an AL Wild Card Series starting Tuesday. Cam Schlittler will start Game 1 on Tuesday, followed by Max Fried and Gerrit Cole.

Aaron Judge appears doubtful for the Wild Card Series because of a calf injury. As of Sunday, Judge's only activity has been plyometric exercises and running on the treadmill.

The Yankees finished 93-67. They were 94-67 in each of the prior two seasons and no team has finished with the same record in three straight seasons, according to the Elias Sports Bureau.

Baltimore finished 79-82 under first-year manager Craig Albernaz, up from 75-87 last year. The Orioles have had consecutive losing seasons after winning 275 games from 2022-24.

The Yankees drew drew 3,297,154 for 79 home dates, down from 3,392,659 in 80 dates last year. They had 12 home sellouts, a drop from 20 last season.

New York never announced its lineup, and the game was canceled about three hours after the scheduled 1:05 p.m. EDT start. This marked the first time since 2002 the Yankees didn't play all 162 games in a non-shortened season.

title: McNulty becomes first US road race world champion since Armstrong
description: Brandon McNulty surprised the favourites in the absence of his team captain Tadej Pogacar to become the first American men's road race cycling world champion in 33 years. McNulty broke with 33 kilometres left and it helped his cause that the top stars such as Olympic champion Remco Evenepoel of Belgium, Isaac del Toro of Mexico and rising Frenchman Paul Seixas joined forces too late to catch him.
fullText:
Brandon McNulty surprised the favourites in the absence of his team captain Tadej Pogacar to become the first American men's road race cycling world champion in 33 years.

McNulty broke with 33 kilometres left and it helped his cause that the top stars such as Olympic champion Remco Evenepoel of Belgium, Isaac del Toro of Mexico and rising Frenchman Paul Seixas joined forces too late to catch him.

McNulty held on win to the race over 273.4 kilometres ahead of Australian Michael Matthews and Dutchman Mathieu van der Poel.

The last American to win the men's road race at the worlds was Lance Armstrong in 1993.

McNulty won the Tour of Poland and the Montreal World Tour last year, and he also has stage wins at the Giro d'Italia and Spanish Vuelta.

Superstar Pogacar was not riding at the Montreal worlds because of injuries he sustained recently at the Vuelta.

fullText:
Tigers news: What Justin Verlander's wife Kate Upton said about his emotional moment to end career appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

The Detroit Tigers bid goodbye to their star pitcher Justin Verlander on Saturday. Verlander got his final start in a Major League Baseball game, going for five-plus innings against the Pittsburgh Pirates. Verlander's wife Kate Upton spoke about what the moment was like when Verlander left the game.

"It was a really emotional day, and the things that mean the most to him were together in one place," Upton said, per The Athletic. "I think that's what made it so special."

Verlander's daughter came out to the mound in the sixth inning, to take Verlander out of the game. The two shared a long hug, and Verlander appeared to get emotional. The Tigers pitcher then fought back tears as he talked to reporters after the game about that moment.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Detroit's crowd also gave Verlander a long ovation. The Tigers would win in a walk-off against the Pirates, 4-3.

"I'm just so grateful for the city and to the fans who love him almost as much as I do," Upton said.

Verlander started just two games for Detroit this season. He will end his 2026 campaign with a 7.00 ERA. Despite his limited time on the mound this season, Verlander soaked in every moment of Saturday's start.

"The vibe in the stadium, from the second I walked out there, was just really incredible," Verlander said, per MLB.com. "It brought back some really fond memories of the days when this ballpark was absolutely raucous every single night."

The Tigers pitcher ends a remarkable career that started more than 20 years ago. He finished his start Saturday with six strikeouts. Verlander now has 3,560 career regular season strikeouts.

Detroit will miss the Major League Baseball Playoffs this season. The Tigers are 76-85 on the campaign. The team will try to end the season with a win on Sunday against the Pirates.

title: Warriors news: Draymond Green hits Michael Porter Jr. with ominous warning after All-Star confession
description: Michael Porter Jr. enjoyed a breakout season with the Brooklyn Nets after spending seven seasons with the Denver Nuggets. However, his performances dropped a few levels after the 28-year-old failed to earn his first All-Star appearance, something he recently claimed was down to a lack of motivation as there was nothing to play for, with the Nets […] The post Warriors news: Draymond Green hits Michael Porter Jr. with ominous warning after All-Star confession appeared first on ClutchPoints.
fullText:
Warriors news: Draymond Green hits Michael Porter Jr. with ominous warning after All-Star confession appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

Michael Porter Jr. enjoyed a breakout season with the Brooklyn Nets after spending seven seasons with the Denver Nuggets. However, his performances dropped a few levels after the 28-year-old failed to earn his first All-Star appearance, something he recently claimed was down to a lack of motivation as there was nothing to play for, with the Nets finishing the season 13th in the East with a 20-62 record.

Now, Draymond Green has fired a warning towards the forward, claiming that teams in the future are likely to hold his drop in performances against him. With Porter Jr. set to enter the final year of his 5-year, $179.3 million max contract, Green believes he will have to play much better in order to convince teams to sign him.

Draymond Green on Michael Porter Jr. admitting he lost motivation after his All-Star snub:

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

“Because he didn’t finish the year strong, people are just like ‘Oh man, he’s just out there playing on a bad team to make an All-Star game.’ Now you’re going to have to play so much… pic.twitter.com/4l0k0bJEw4

— NBABase (@TheNBABase) September 26, 2026

"Because he didn't finish the year strong, people are just like 'Oh man, he's just out there playing on a bad team to make an All-Star game,'" Green said. "Now you're going to have to play so much better… teams looking to sign him are going to hold this against him in the future."

Porter Jr. finished the season with averages of 24.2 points, 7.1 rebounds and three assists per game while shooting at almost 37% from the three-point zone. However, he was shooting at almost 40% before the All-Star break while averaging close to 26 points per game, which dropped to around 21 points post the snub.

The Nets star himself claimed that with the Nets out of playoff contention, he let his 'foot off the gas.'

"We couldn't make the playoffs, I couldn't be an All-Star, so I let my foot off the gas. I wasn't in the weight room as much, I wasn't preparing as much, and my three-point percentage dropped. But even the crazy shots I was shooting this year, I still was almost 40%," he said.

Green, who himself is a four-time All-Star believes that the drop is bound to make teams believe that he was playing on a 'bad team' merely to ensure that he ends up earning his first All-Star selection. Now, Porter Jr. will indeed need to return to his pre-snub form, especially if he wants teams to show interest when and if he eventually becomes a free agent at the end of the coming season.

title: Will Liverpool Win A PL Title Now That Man City Have Been Found Guilty Of Breaching FFP Rules?
description: In a recent report, the Athletic revealed that Manchester City have been found guilty of violating the Premier League’s 114 of 115 Financial Fair Play regulations. After a verdict was reached by an ...
fullText:
In a recent report, the Athletic revealed that Manchester City have been found guilty of violating the Premier League's 114 of 115 Financial Fair Play regulations. After a verdict was reached by an independent panel, the Mancunian club were found to be at fault for breaching all but one of the Premier League FFP rules. However, any official sanctions are yet to be finalised.

The Etihad-based outfit remain determined to prove their innocence, but the formal process regarding their charges are still ongoing. Following an investigation into reported breaches between 2009 and 2018, Man City were found guilty. During that period, the Mancunian club lifted three Premier League titles. However, only time will tell whether they get stripped of any of their league titles when the sanctions are determined.

Liverpool secured a runners-up finish once in Man City's title-winning seasons between 2009 and 2018. In the 2013-14 campaign, the Reds finished with 84 points, just a couple of points short of first-placed Man City. Hence, the Merseyside club would be keen on hearing about any sanctions imposed by the Premier League following the Mancunian club's guilty verdict.

BOURNEMOUTH, ENGLAND – SEPTEMBER 20: Andoni Iraola, Manager of Liverpool, and Marco Rose, Manager of Bournemouth, embrace before the Premier League 2026/27 match between AFC Bournemouth and Liverpool FC at Vitality Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Bournemouth, England. (Photo by Steve Bardens/Getty Images)

Liverpool could potentially win one more league title, which would take their total tally to 21. The lure of having another Premier League trophy in their cabinet could be too lucrative to turn down for the Merseyside club.

Liverpool would fancy their chances of bagging another league title if the Premier League decide to make an example of Man City after their 114 FFP breaches.

The sheer amount of violations could see the Mancunian club get a heavy points-deduction. Relegation to the lower leagues of English football and stripping them of their league titles, might also be on the cards if Man City fail to prove their innocence.

Either way, the Reds should consider launching an appeal to overturn their runners-up finish from the 2013-14 season. The Liverpool fans are proud of their history and having another league title in their cabinet would only help the Merseyside club attract more top players and build towards a brighter future.

title: Fantasy Football Week 4 Early Waiver Wire Pickups: Ollie Gordon II, Braelon Allen top adds after De'Von Achane, Breece Hall injuries
description: We're looking ahead to Week 4 fantasy football waiver wire adds.
fullText:
As we get deeper into the 2026 fantasy football season, the viable options off the waiver wire are going to get pretty thin. Injuries are going to open things up for most of the top adds moving forward, and going into Week 4, that's precisely the case. We're here to get you ahead of the game and ready to make your waiver plans. Below are some early pickups off the waiver wire to consider as we approach the end of Week 3.

The Dolphins are tracking to be one of the worst teams in the NFL this season. That doesn't mean they can't have at least a few viable fantasy football options. Perhaps the only one was RB De'Von Achane, who exited in the first quarter versus the Chiefs in Week 3 due to a knee injury. While we don't know the severity or if Achane will miss time, if that is the case, we know Gordon's role will increase plenty.

After Achane left the contest, Gordon immediately scored a touchdown on what was one of Miami's best drives of the past six seasons. He ended up finishing the game with 17 carries for 41 yards and a touchdown (3 catches, 14 yards) for 13.4 fantasy points. Gordon was forced to exit late in the game due to cramps but was able to return.

If Achane is sidelined, Gordon becomes one of the top adds for Week 4 and would offer RB3/flex value with upside. The Dolphins may not be in many run-positive game scripts but Gordon would still be in line for plenty of snaps/touches. Jaylen Wright was inactive in Week 3 and DJ Herman likely wouldn't command many (if any) touches.

Speaking of injured RB1s, Breece Hall had to leave in the second half versus the Lions after being tackled awkwardly and was ruled out with a thigh injury. That type of injury doesn't scream long-term absence, but we have to get some more information on Hall.

Braelon Allen is the next man up for the Jets in the backfield and we know he can make plays when called upon. He had 334 rushing yards, 19 catches for 148 yards and three TDs as a rookie a few seasons ago. If Hall is out, Allen should take over as the lead back with Isaiah Davis mixing in. The Jets face the Bears and Browns the next few weeks, and if Hall sits, Allen would be an RB2/3 in PPR formats.

We haven't had many rookies make a big impact so far in 2026 but Sadiq may carve out a solid role on this improved Jets offense. Sadiq got his second career TD, and first as a receiver, in Week 3 versus the Lions. He'd finish the game with seven receptions for 105 yards and the TD for 20 fantasy points.

Geno Smith looks great throwing behind this revamped offensive line. There are more mouths to feed than we expected in New York but Sadiq could develop chemistry with the veteran QB while WRs Omar Cooper Jr. and Adonai Mitchell are sidelined. The Jets also could be without Garrett Wilson, who left late in the game after taking a big hit.

We're almost into the start of bye weeks (Week 5), so Sadiq isn't a bad add if you need depth at tight end or a streaming option with TE1 upside.

title: Josh Allen closing in on Buffalo Bills history after second rushing touchdown
description: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen is now close to some team history.
fullText:
The Buffalo Bills, particularly their offense led by star quarterback Josh Allen, have looked fantastic to start the 2026 NFL season. After Week 3, they are 3-0 and have scored a league-leading 101 points.

Sunday's Week 3 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers at home marked their second game at the new Highmark Stadium. After a slow start offensively, Allen and the Bills started to make some progress in the second half.

Midway through the fourth quarter, Allen ran into the end zone for a 1-yard touchdown that put the Bills in front 17-13. As reported by the Bills' official PR account on X, that touchdown was the 87th from scrimmage in his career. That ties franchise legends Thurman Thomas and Andre Reed for the most in team history.

85 of those scores have been on the ground with two coming through the air. This accomplishment is especially impressive considering that Allen is a QB, whereas Thomas and Reed played skill positions.

On a day where Allen did not look his best passing (16-for-26, 204 yards, two interceptions) he was able to make some important carries. He rushed seven times for 23 yards, adding two touchdowns.

Allen is now on the brink of Buffalo franchise history, a team that has existed since the 1970 merger. His next opportunity to achieve that 88th scrimmage touchdown will come next Sunday in Week 4 versus their division rival New England Patriots.

title: Lawrence throws 3 TD passes as Jaguars rout Patriots and raise more questions about Maye
description: Trevor Lawrence threw three touchdown passes, including one on which Parker Washington made a fingertip catch in the end zone, and the Jacksonville Jaguars bounced back from their worst offensive performance in nearly a year to dominate New England 35-6.
fullText:
Trevor Lawrence threw three touchdown passes, including one on which Parker Washington made a fingertip catch in the end zone, and the Jacksonville Jaguars bounced back from their worst offensive performance in nearly a year to dominate New England 35-6 on Sunday.

Lawrence also strangely gave himself up at the 1-yard line with nearly 9 minutes to play. It created countless laughs on the sideline. Bhayshul Tuten scored on the next play, which surely will cause angst in the fantasy football world.

Regardless, the Jaguars (2-1) won their sixth consecutive regular-season game at home and raised more questions about Drake Maye's regression for the Patriots.

Maye fumbled twice, losing one, and threw two more interceptions before getting pulled in the fourth quarter with the game out of reach. He now has one TD pass and six INTs in three games. He threw 31 touchdowns and eight picks last season for the AFC champion Patriots (1-2).

Maye's performance in this one was more alarming than his three-interception fourth quarter in the season opener at Seattle. The ball slipped out of his right hand with no one around him during one play. He threw into coverage on a third-and-goal play, resulting in Travis Hunter's first career interception. He also threw a pass directly to cornerback Jarrian Jones that set up another score for Jacksonville.

New England had other issues, too: Andy Borregales missed a 38-yard field goal; Kyle Williams mistakenly stepped out of bounds on a kickoff return, giving the Pats the ball at their 9-yard line; and Mack Hollins was flagged for taunting at the end of a 9-yard reception, turning a fourth-and-1 play into a field-goal situation.

The Jaguars were much cleaner all afternoon.

Lawrence completed 19 of 29 passes for 182 yards, with an interception on a tipped pass. He connected with Jakobi Meyers and Josh Cameron for TDs. Cameron got significant snaps in place of Brian Thomas Jr., who dropped two passes in last week's 20-13 loss at Denver.

Tuten finished with 73 yards rushing.

Facing a first-and-30 play after back-to-back penalties, the Patriots dialed up some trickiness in Jacksonville territory. And it worked despite a lot of adversity.

Maye threw a backward pass to Elton Chism III, who had to elude Jones' tackle near the sideline. Chism stayed on his feet and completed a pass to Mack Hollins that was tipped by cornerback Travis Hunter. It was far from pretty but resulted in a 16-yard gain that led to a field goal.

Jacksonville's Cam Little just missed making a 70-yard field goal, which would have broken his NFL record. Little attempted the long kick at the end of the first half and pushed it just a couple feet right.

Little had the distance, which was no surprise considering he made a 70-yard in a preseason game against Pittsburgh in 2025. He set the real NFL mark later that year with a 68-yarder at Las Vegas in early November.

Patriots: RG Greg Van Roten left in the first half with a thigh injury and did not return. DT Christian Barmore (shoulder) and CB Carlton Davis III also missed snaps but later returned.

Jaguars: DT DaVon Hamilton stayed on the ground in pain after sacking Maye but was able to return a few plays later.

Patriots: Play at Buffalo next Sunday.

Jaguars: Play at Cincinnati next Sunday.

This is a developing story. Check back for updates as more information becomes available.

title: Bills overcome five turnovers to defeat Chargers, 24-16
description: While it was ugly for much of the afternoon, Buffalo was still able to defeat Los Angeles and move to 3-0.
fullText:
It's not often that a team can turn the ball over five times and win.

But that's exactly what happened in Buffalo on Sunday, with the Bills coming from behind to defeat the Chargers 24-16.

Los Angeles was able to get off to a 10-0 lead after a fumble from James Cook on the first play from scrimmage and an interception on Buffalo's third drive.

But the Bills were able to tie it up at 10-10 with Josh Allen's 1-yard touchdown run late in the second quarter. Allen had set it up with a 37-yard pass to Keon Coleman with little time before the break.

The Bills had three turnovers in the first half. While they had two more fumbles in the second half, the Chargers punted after one and Justin Herbert threw an interception deep in the red zone on the second.

Josh Allen powered his way in for another 1-yard touchdown with 7:35 left in the contest to give the Bills their first lead of the day. Then James Cook was actually allowed to run in a touchdown, taking it in from 3 yards out to put the game away.

Aside from his fumble, Cook had an excellent day — rushing for 154 yards on 24 carries with his TD.

Allen finished 16-of-26 for 204 yards with two interceptions and a lost fumble. He had 22 yards on eight carries with two TDs.

On the other side, Herbert was 20-of-34 for 226 yards with a touchdown and an interception.

That was Los Angeles' lone giveaway of the game, but the +4 advantage in turnover margin was not enough.

With the victory, the Bills are now 3-0. They'll stay at home to host the Patriots next Sunday.

The Chargers are 0-3 and staring down the barrel of a long season. They will be on the road to face the defending-champion Seahawks next Sunday.

title: Too little, too late for Cam Ward and Titans in deflating loss to Giants | Estes
description: A stirring comeback attempt couldn't salvage a game the Titans' offense didn't show up to play until late in the third quarter.
fullText:
Rapid reaction from the Tennessee Titans' ugly and rainy 12-7 road loss to the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium:

First, it was awful. Then, it suddenly got a lot better. Then, it still wasn't enough. That was Cam Ward's afternoon. While it included a stirring comeback bid, it'll be remembered for a bad decision and an interception in the end zone in the final seconds, preserving a victory for the Giants. They won despite failing to score a touchdown and being outgained by the Titans, 262 yards to 238. For the Titans, this loss was full of missed opportunities and subpar football, yet they had a chance at the end. Falling to 0-3 in such a fashion is going to sting.

-In this odd matchup of former coaches for both teams, Dennard Wilson held on to get the win. With an assist from the wet weather, the Giants' defensive coordinator (and former Titans DC) dominated his old team's offense and Ward for much of the game. Offensively, the Titans barely did anything until late in the third quarter, when they advanced inside the Giants' 10-yard line, only to turn it over on downs. The Titans finally scored with 5:35 remaining, but it wasn't enough as the final drive ended with Ward's interception. The Titans' final four offensive possessions all advanced into Giants territory, yet only one resulted in points.

It was just too little, too late from Ward. He finally got into a rhythm in the fourth quarter, leading a 91-yard touchdown drive, capped by a 4-yard TD pass to Wan'Dale Robinson. The Titans should've scored on the possession prior to the TD, but they instead turned it over on downs at the Giants' 7-yard line. On fourth-and-5, Ward tossed a pass out of the back of the end zone, giving no one a chance to come down with it. And then . . . there was the game-ending interception.

The Giants' offense, coordinated by Matt Nagy (who missed out on the Titans' head coaching job that went to Robert Saleh), wasn't a polished operation with Jameis Winston stepping in for an injured Jaxson Dart. But they were able to run well enough to at least move the football and score points during the first three quarters, which built a hefty advantage in possession time.

The sophomore slump is real for Chimere Dike, whose fumble on the opening kickoff made it two in three games and set a tone for this fiasco. The Titans know they have an All Pro-caliber return man, but how many more fumbles will it take to consider other options back there?

Rookie right guard Fernando Carmona Jr. hurt his ankle on the Titans' first offensive snap and didn't return. Jackson Slater, who got passed by Carmona during the preseason, was tapped to replace him.

The game was up for grabs until Ward threw it to the Giants' Jevon Holland.

1 – First downs gained by the Titans in the first half. And it took nearly 29 minutes of football to get the one. The Titans went three-and-punt on their first five offensive possessions, gaining a grand total of 22 net yards.

The Titans' defense wasn't spectacular, but it continued to fight to keep the Giants out of the end zone, forcing field goals and keeping the Titans in this game while their offense floundered.

The Titans need more from Ward. He was beaten by a rusty, out-of-form Winston. Sadly, struggles are becoming the norm for the former No. 1 overall draft pick, with success as the exception.

title: Henry Cejudo: 'Deen The B*tch' owes me a f*cking fight'
description: Henry Cejudo wants Misfits Boxing to re-book his fight against 'Deen The Great.'
fullText:
Henry Cejudo is not ready to run the page on Nurideen Shabazz, aka "Deen The Great."

The former two-division UFC champion wants to get rebooked against Deen following a victory in his professional boxing debut. Cejudo defeated "Euphoria" actor Javon Walton via split decision in the main event of Misfits Boxing 11, which went down on Saturday night in Miami. He was originally scheduled to fight Deen, who pulled out of the fight with an injury.

Cejudo feels a rebooking against Deen makes the most sense next.

"First and foremost, I think Deen 'The Duck' owes me a f*cking fight," Cejudo told Fred Talks Fighting. "That's what he does, and it's time for me to put that duck to sleep. You guys have to stop calling him 'Deen The Great,' it's 'Deen The B*tch.' Why don't we call him that? He needs to show up, and we have to throw down because that was the original plan. If he can't do that, then just stream; don't talk your sh*t. You're not a boxer then. If you're not willing to fight, then just stream and have fun kissing your boyfriend Adrien 'Boner' (Adrien Broner)."

Cejudo, who retired from MMA in December 2025, thinks Deen faked an injury to avoid fighting him. It annoys him that Deen labels himself as a boxer, as he sees him more as a streamer.

"Deen, just step up, bro," Cejudo said. "If you're not about it, just start streaming. You're not hurt; you're not injured. Nobody believes you, including me and everyone you know here at Misfits. If you're not about it, just sit the hell down, and that's it. If you're trying to scrap and you mean it, then let's do it then. If not, just shut the hell up. That's all I got to say."

title: 3 games, 3 wins: Joe Brady makes NFL history
description: At 37, Brady became the fifth-youngest NFL head coach to win his first three games
fullText:
Joe Brady is three games into his NFL head-coaching career, and he still hasn't lost one.

The Buffalo Bills beat the Los Angeles Chargers 24-16 on Sunday, improving to 3-0 under Brady and putting their new head coach in some pretty exclusive company in the process.

At 37 years old, Brady became the fifth-youngest head coach in NFL history to begin his career with three straight wins. Only Josh McDaniels, John Madden, Bill Cowher, and Mike Tomlin were younger when they started 3-0.

McDaniels and Madden were both 33 when they reached the mark, while Cowher and Tomlin were 35.

Brady had already made a little franchise history one week earlier. Buffalo's win over Detroit made him the first head coach in Bills history to win each of his first two regular-season games at the helm. Sunday's win pushed the streak to three and moved the accomplishment beyond the Buffalo record book.

Brady turned 37 on Wednesday, making him the youngest active head coach in the NFL. According to Bills PR, he is also the second-youngest head coach or manager across the NFL, MLB, NBA, and NHL, behind only 34-year-old Washington Nationals manager Blake Butera.

Bills HC Joe Brady turns 37 today. 

Brady is the youngest active HC in the NFL and is the second-youngest coach across the MLB/NBA/NFL/NHL, behind only Washington Nationals' manager Blake Butera (34 years old). pic.twitter.com/aJdPRmBxiZ

Brady took over as Buffalo's head coach after spending the previous two-plus seasons running the Bills' offense, first as interim offensive coordinator during the 2023 season and then in the permanent role.

Now, three games into his first head-coaching job, Brady has three wins. That means his usual postgame message needs another update.

title: Buffalo Bills stock report: horns up/horns down vs. Los Angeles Chargers
description: It was an ugly win, but Buffalo prevailed in a 24-16 slugfest
fullText:
The Buffalo Bills fought hard against the Los Angeles Chargers, weathering a first half period of horrendous play before settling into what was ultimately a very competitive football game. After falling into a 10-0 hole early on, the Bills were able to tie it up at 10 before the end of the first half.

A series of miscues throughout the game prevented Buffalo from gaining any sort of momentum, however, until the fourth quarter. The Bills added two second half turnovers to the three they committed in the first half, limiting any positive progress that the team made on offense.

Eventually, the Buffalo offense fought through that early malaise, doing just enough to pull out an ugly, hard-fought win over a motivated Chargers team desperate to avoid an 0-3 start. While Buffalo trailed into the fourth quarter, the Bills ultimately prevailed, digging deep for a 24-13 win and a 3-0 start to the 2026 NFL season.

The Bills aren't going to put much of today's game on any highlight reels, but an ugly win is always better than a pretty loss. There were plenty of ups and downs today, and we've done the best we can to reflect the roller coaster ride in our stock report for this one. 
_____________________________________________________________________________

Horns Down: Offensive Preparedness

It was a sloppy first quarter, and that's putting it kindly. On Buffalo's first offensive play, James Cook lost a fumble, negating the advantage given to the Bills by Greg Dortch's excellent opening kickoff return. It also gifted the Chargers a short field, which they took advantage of in the form of a short passing touchdown to running back Keaton Mitchell. After a punt on their second possession, the Bills third possession came to a quick end when Josh Allen misread the Chargers' defensive coverage and threw an interception directly into the hands of safety Genesis Smith, which led to a Chargers field goal and a 10-0 first quarter lead. A holding penalty on Alec Anderson and some poor blocking from Connor McGovern and O'Cyrus Torrence also had Buffalo on the ropes early. It was a horrendous starts for a Buffalo offense that had been exceptional in its first two outings.

Horns Down: First Half Josh Allen

With Allen, turnovers tend to come in bunches or not at all. Unfortunately, that trend continued, as Allen threw his first interception on a bad read. Then, on the ensuing possession, Allen made another boneheaded decision, throwing into triple coverage deep down field in an attempt to let DJ Moore make a play. Granted, it took an absolute fluke play for Genesis Smith to come down with his second interception of the day, but the decision to throw the ball was not a great one. After two nearly flawless games to open the year, Allen played about as poorly as he could have to start the game. It wasn't pretty, but he cleaned it up as the day went on, eventually leading the Bills on long scoring drives that gave Buffalo the victory. Allen completed 16-of-26 passes for 204 yards. He also rushed eight times for 22 yards and two scores. His three turnovers were an issue, but the Bills were able to do enough to overcome them.

Greg Dortch looked good on kickoff returns, averaging nearly 31 yards per try. Sam Franklin Jr. was a demon on kick coverage, notching two tackles and sticking his nose in plenty of tough spots. Tyler Bass hit all three of his PATs and his lone field goal try, a 28-yard boot. Tommy Doman Jr. drilled a 51-yard punt. Overall, the special teams unit led by special teams coach Jeff Rodgers has been a positive for the team.

Groot has been incredible this season, and he made his presence known early in today's game. He made a few solid run stuffs on plays to the outside, and he also brought a first-half drive to an end by notching Buffalo's first sack on Justin Herbert. That was Rousseau's fifth sack of the season, continuing what has been an outstanding start to the year for Buffalo's 2021 first-round pick. Rousseau's career high for sacks in a season is eight; at this pace, he's going to race by that before the Bills' bye in Week Seven. He added another sack in the second half to give him six on the year, and he notched eight tackles, including four tackles for loss, in today's win.

Playing through a painful shoulder injury isn't an easy task, but Moore was huge for the Bills in the first half. We already talked about the bad Allen force on what turned out to be an unlucky interception (a play where Allen might have thought he had a free play with a Chargers player offside), but Moore was able to find space and move the chains for Allen and the offense on the team's first touchdown drive. Moore converted two huge third downs on that two-minute drive, catching a 13-yard pass on third-and-four before the two minute warning, and then another 10-yard pass to convert a third-and-seven on the other side of the two minute warning. Moore added one other grab on the drive, which ended with a one-yard Josh Allen plunge. Moore looked good throughout the afternoon, catching six passes for 67 yards on a team-high ten targets.

I feel like a broken record hammering the same point over and over, but Benford has played poorly all season. He's losing in coverage when the team plays man, finding himself in trail position far too often. He also committed a huge holding penalty (that was, if you're asking a biased Bills fan like myself, not a foul) to negate what would have been a big interception from C.J. Gardner-Johnson. Granted, the Bills defense held the Chargers to a field goal, but the difference between holding the team to three points or no points at all is huge in the grand scheme of a Sunday. I think it's fair to wonder whether Benford is miscast in new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard's defense. He went down with an injury late in the third quarter, and it was announced that he was questionable to return with a toe injury. I hope I'm overreacting to a poor stretch of play, but Benford needs to be better overall.

The rookie looked excellent in relief of Benford, notching a pass breakup on the second play after No. 47 left with his injury. He also was strong in run support, totaling six tackles on the afternoon, most of which came near the line of scrimmage. There was speculation that Igbinosun was drafted to provide competition for second-year man Maxwell Hairston, but today, he proved to be a more-than-capable replacement for Benford.

Yes, he had that one negative play to start the game. However, as the afternoon wore on, the Chargers run defense had few answers for him. Cook continually found big chunks on the ground, and he was able to get out some tough yards between the tackles, as well. Buffalo's offensive line settled as the day wore on, especially in run blocking, which gave Cook plenty of room to operate. He totaled 21 carries for 141 yards and a big-time touchdown in the fourth quarter to ice the game.

The veteran had an interception overturned by a questionable penalty on Christian Benford, but then he made up for it later, ending a potentially back-breaking Chargers drive by intercepting Justin Herbert in the end zone on a third down early in the fourth quarter. Gardner-Johnson's long return put the Buffalo offense in great position, and it could have been even better had a facemask penalty been called as he was tackled. Overall, Gardner-Johnson was a bright spot in the secondary, which was a positive sign after two weeks of middling play from the veteran. Gardner-Johnson had five tackles and two pass breakups to go with the aforementioned interception.

I feel bad for Skarekrow this week. On the bright side, he'll have plenty to work with…but, it was a bad day for the Bills in terms of penalties, and it was also a bad day for the zebras throwing (and not throwing, in some cases) those flags.

Regardless of the result of the game, those things are hideous.

Horns Unknown: You Make the Call

What do you think, friends? Who deserves some praise—and who deserves more criticism? Let us know in the comments below.

title: Bills overcome 5 turnovers, sluggish start to overcome Chargers in ugly game
description: The Bills were down early and trailed in the fourth quarter, but Josh Allen and the offense overcame a sluggish game to top the Chargers.
fullText:
The Buffalo Bills are fortunate to be 3-0 after the winless Los Angeles Chargers gave them a scare at Highmark Stadium on Sunday.

The Bills were in a 10-0 hole early and trailed in the fourth quarter, but Josh Allen led two fourth-quarter TD drives against a plucky Chargers team that had struggled in their first two home games.

It was all Chargers early, but they dropped to 0-3 with the 24-16 loss. They scored on their opening drive but were held out of the end zone for the game's final 50-plus minutes.

The Bills were all out of sorts offensively early, coming up empty on their first four drives. Allen was intercepted on the last two of those, with the picks coming on back-to-back pass attempts — both by Chargers rookie safety Genesis Smith for his first two NFL picks. That allowed the Chargers to build an early 10-0 lead. It should have been 13-0, but Chargers kicker missed a 45-yard field-goal try.

Buffalo capitalized with 10 points on two drives to close out the first half, with Allen taking in his first rushing score of the day to tie the game at halftime.

The Chargers took back control briefly with a field goal. The Bills then turned it over twice, with Dalton Kincaid and Allen each coughing up fumbles. The upset alert appeared to be fully on at this point.

But the Bills capitalized on a Herbert interception, with Allen's touchdown capping a 13-play drive for a 17-13 Buffalo lead. Then after the Chargers turned the ball over on downs in their own territory, the Bills pushed the lead to 24-13 on James Cook's rushing score.

A late Dicker field goal made it a one-score game, but the Bills recovered the onsides kick and ran out the clock.

The Bills were fortunate to win this game. They lost the turnover battle, 5-1 (or 5-2, if you count turnovers on downs), and had an interception and a touchdown called back by penalties. Buffalo was flagged 10 times for 88 yards and had multiple flags declined.

Buffalo allowed a Dicker field goal after the dropped pick. But Allen and the Bills' offense converted a touchdown after Ty Johnson's fourth-down score was wiped out. The Bills were fortunate that the Chargers couldn't capitalize better on their mistakes.

title: Titans comeback falls short as Cam Ward tossed last-second INT vs. Giants
description: The Tennessee Titans fell, 12-7, to the New York Giants after a late interception by Cam Ward in rainy conditions.
fullText:
The Tennessee Titans got nothing going against the New York Giants and once again came up short, falling 12-7 at rainy MetLife Stadium in Week 3 action.

Cam Ward and the offense did come to life in the second half to make it close. But two failed trips into the red zone, including throwing a game-sealing interception in the waning seconds, did the Titans in.

The Titans' defense played another strong game, but the lack of offense in the first half did them in.

Weather: With a nor'easter plaguing the Northeast, conditions at MetLife Stadium were sloppy, and the Giants took advantage by controlling the line of scrimmage, controlling the ball, and winning field-position battles.

Penalties: Any time the Titans got anything going, they committed a penalty that set them back. In a game where field position and ball control mattered, Tennessee got the worst of it.

First half offense: The Titans offense again couldn't get anything going and wasted a solid game from the defense, which, despite the score, did everything it could to keep Tennessee in the game. In a game where every yard mattered, the Titans' offense couldn't make the play when it mattered.

Turnovers: The Titans committed two turnovers against the Giants, and they both came at inopportune times: on the opening kickoff and in the end zone with 17 seconds left in the contest.

Cam Ward threw a game-sealing interception with 17 seconds remaining. The Titans had two timeouts remaining, and instead of living to play another down, Ward tried to force the ball to Elic Ayomanor and threw the pick.

Jeffery Simmons: Simmons was again a man on a mission and was his dominant self. He finished with 10 tackles and one sack, but his impact went far beyond the box score. The emotional leader of the defense, he stepped up every time Tennessee needed a play.

Tommy Townsend: Townsend came through and consistently helped change field position when called upon. The veteran punter needed to be a weapon in the weather, and he was.

Wan'Dale Robinson: Robinson had his best game with the Titans, and although it was not a huge statistical day, he was a focal part of the offense and made even more plays than his stat line would indicate. He led the Titans with seven catches for 58 yards and one touchdown.

The Titans suffered a massive loss early when starting guard Fernando Carmona injured his ankle and did not return. Cornerback Alontae Taylor and running back Tyjae Spears both left the game with injuries, but returned to action.

Titans head coach Robert Saleh will meet with reporters on Monday afternoon to wrap up the week and set the stage for Week 4. Select players may be made available after Saleh's press conference.

Tennessee will return to practice on Wednesday ahead of a Week 4 game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore, Maryland. Kickoff is scheduled for Noon CDT.

title: Vikings up 10-0 after Myles Price punt return TD
description: The NFL's first punt return touchdown of the 2026 season belongs to Vikings wide receiver Myles Price.
fullText:
The NFL's first punt return touchdown of the 2026 season belongs to Vikings wide receiver Myles Price.

Price fielded a Riley Dixon punt at his own 14-yard line and broke loose for an 86-yard score. The touchdown pushed the Vikings' lead to 10-0 with 8:43 left to play in the first quarter.

It was the first touchdown of Price's NFL career.

The Vikings opened the scoring with a seven-play, 40-yard drive that ended with a Will Reichard field goal. Wide receiver Justin Jefferson caught two passes for 32 yards from Kyler Murray on the drive. Murray is returning after being cleared from his Week 1 concussion.

title: Blue screen? Brazil's World Cup villain makes bizarre errors v Portugal
description: Orjan Nyland was one of the Brazilian National Team’s tormentors at the last World Cup.He saved the penalty taken by Bruno Guimarães and made other crucial stops that helped eliminate Ancelotti’s...
fullText:
Orjan Nyland was one of the Brazilian national team's tormentors at the last World Cup.

He saved the penalty taken by Bruno Guimarães and made other crucial saves that helped seal the elimination of Ancelotti's side.

And the Norway goalkeeper has been in the spotlight "for the wrong reasons" in this Sunday's (27) clash against Portugal.

Which is part of League A of the UEFA Nations League.

Now an RB Leipzig player after facing Brazil while unattached, Nyland made two bad mistakes against Gonçalo Ramos.

And he was only saved by VAR on one occasion.

Norway had just equalized through Haaland (51'), after João Félix opened the scoring in the 17th minute.

Then Nyland tried to play out from the back with Odegaard.

But the pass was too short, Gonçalo Ramos was alert and chipped the goalkeeper to put Portugal back in front (54').

It took only five minutes for them to cross paths again on the pitch.

Nyland tried to get there before the Milan striker, but miskicked it. And he paid the price.

But VAR stepped in and confirmed an offside position.

Much to Nyland's relief in the match, which is still underway in Oslo.

title: Yankees' game against Orioles canceled, ending 2026 regular season with 93-68 record as Wild Card Series looms

fullText:
The Yankees' 2026 regular season is in the books. Sunday's 1:05 p.m. game at Yankee Stadium between New York and the Baltimore Orioles, which was originally moved up from 3:20 p.m., is canceled due to inclement weather.

"The game will not be rescheduled," the Yankees said in part of a release.

Thirty-three minutes before the game's original start time, the Yankees announced on X, "Please be advised today's game will not start on time."

After more than three hours without an update, the game was called.

title: Jaguars Hand Patriots Its Worst Loss Since 2024
description: The Jaguars send a statement at home, dominating the Patriots, handing New England its worst loss since 2024.
fullText:
The Jacksonville Jaguars had something to prove following their Week 2 road loss to the Denver Broncos. They did that and then some, proving they belong with a dominant, 29-point blowout of the reigning AFC Super Bowl runner-up, the New England Patriots. Trevor Lawrence had an efficient day, spreading the ball to nine different pass catchers, while the defense completely shut the Patriots out of the end zone.

Here's everything you need to know from Jacksonville's Week 3 home domination of the New England Patriots.

After both teams' early defensive success, which included three consecutive punts, Patriots quarterback Drake Maye made the day's first mistake. With the Patriots moving down the field into scoring range, Maye turned the ball over, fumbling it back to Jacksonville to end the drive.

On 1st and 10 from Jacksonville's 35, Drake May Will Levis's it, fumbling the ball back to Jacksonville while resting in a clean pocket for the game's first turnover
 pic.twitter.com/IXCsOIYOoO

After the turnover, the Jacksonville offense put together the game's first score on a 10-play, 62-yard, 5:27 drive, highlighted by explosive catches from Parker Washington (18 yards) and Josh Cameron's 12-yard touchdown catch. However, the first-half turnovers didn't just belong to Maye, as one series later, Lawrence's pass to Brenton Strange was dropped/deflected by the tight end and intercepted by New England cornerback Marcus Jones. The turnover in their own end of the field cost Jacksonville just three points, with the defense holding New England to just three yards on the drive, however.

Marcus Jones snags the INT for the @Patriots!@NEvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/zqdcfMuhxV

The Jacksonville offense picked up where it left off before the turnover, putting together a nine-play, 62-yard touchdown drive highlighted by a 23-yard Brenton Strange catch and capped by Jakobi Meyer's redzone touchdown.

What a DOT 🎯 #NEvsJAX on CBS & @paramountplus pic.twitter.com/c4khecQOX1

New England, driving to the Jacksonville two-yard line, looked ready to cut the Jaguars' lead to one-possession when Maye suffered his second turnover of the first half – this one, a third-down, redzone, attempt directly to cornerback Travis Hunter. This was Hunter's first career interception, saving a touchdown.

Jacksonville was unable to turn the ensuing drive into points, as the Cam Little 70-yard field goal, with time expiring, sailed wide right. However, the kick, against the wind, somehow still had the length.

QB Trevor Lawrence ended the half 13 of 20 with 111 yards, two touchdowns, and 1 interception (91.9 passer rating). RB Bhayshul Tuten had 8 carries for 48-yards (6.0 per carry).

Following the half, New England's day of mistakes continued, to the joy of the Jaguar faithful. After a 10-play, 42-yard drive, Patriots kicker Andy Borregales missed a chip-shot 38-yard kick.

The Jaguars' offense continued their onslaught, compiling a 15-play, 72-yard drive capped by an impossible 17-yard Parker Washington catch while being interfered with. Immediately following the ensuing kickoff, cornerback Jarrian Jones continued the turnover party, securing his first interception of the year. Chris Rodriguez scored on a five-yard rush on the next play. This score resulted in a 28-3 lead and effectively sealed the Jacksonville victory.

.@Jaguars with another INT 🔥@NEvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/h2HW8rZ2oZ

Special Teams: WR Josh Cameron: 42-yard kick return, plus a kickoff coverage tackle one play after his receiving touchdown

Offense: QB Trevor Lawrence: 19/29 for 182 yards, 6.3 average, 3 touchdowns, 1 interception, 102.9 passer rating. As efficient as he could be, this was essentially a four-touchdown day, as Lawrence purposefully stopped short of scoring in the fourth quarter. Tuten scored on the following snap.

While Sunday's matchup may not have been perfect, it would be hard to identify a more dominant Week 3 performance on the scoreboard, as the Jacksonville defense consistently gave New England quarterback Drake Maye fits in the secondary. While the pass rush occasionally gave Maye slightly more time to scan the field when rushing four, the back end forced two interceptions, with Maye surrendering a third unforced turnover. Offensively, Jacksonville did what good teams do, capitalizing on a struggling opponent's mistakes. The Jaguars won the turnover battle while also winning in points off turnovers, 14-3.

2. BTJ Moving Down The Depth Chart?

Rookie receiver Josh Cameron notably received many of the opening-half third-receiver snaps over third-year, 2024 rookie-of-the-year finalist Brian Thomas Jr. following a rough Week 2 performance featuring two dropped passes. Meanwhile, Cameron secured his second career red zone touchdown against the Patriots, entrenching himself as a bona fide red zone target for this offense. Meanwhile, Thomas received just one target against New England, an eight-yard catch.

Travis Hunter's day started off rough with the second-year dual-threat athlete surrendering an opening-drive 21-yard catch to Patriots receiver Mack Hollins. However, on a day when he noticeably played more snaps than in prior weeks on defense, he also secured his first career interception. This one was a red-zone, touchdown-saving catch.

title: Colts kick late FG to pull out 19-17 win over Texans
description: Colts kicker Spender Shrader, who injured his groin in pregame warmups, ended up playing the part of hero.
fullText:
Colts kicker Spender Shrader, who injured his groin in pregame warmups, ended up playing the part of hero. He kicked field goals of 39, 58, 37 and 53 in the Colts' 19-17 victory over the Texans.

His final field goal came with 16 seconds left.

The Colts are now 1-2, while the Texans fell to 0-3 for the second consecutive season. Houston rallied to make the playoffs last season, but the odds are against them to do it again.

The Colts, who led 13-7 at halftime and 16-7 midway through the fourth quarter, had the lead until 1:48 remained. C.J. Stroud directed a seven-play, 54-yard drive with Woody Marks scoring on a 1-yard run.

The Texans, though, botched the kickoff, with Ka'imi Fairbairn kicking it into the end zone. That allowed the Colts to start their game-winning drive at their own 35. DeMeco Ryans then botched the clock management, failing to use his first timeout after Jonathan Taylor's run left more than a minute on the clock.

Ryans finally called the timeout with 29 seconds remaining. It left too little time for the Texans to get into field goal range, and Stroud's Hail Mary throw on the final play was both short and out of bounds.

The Colts outgained the Texans 300 to 223 yards, with Daniel Jones going 24-of-36 for 235 yards with a touchdown and an interception. He also lost two fumbles, though the Texans turned it over on downs after the first one.

Jonathan Taylor had 23 carries for 68 yards, and Josh Downs caught five passes for 77 yards.

Adetomiwa Adebawore and DeForest Buckner each had 1 1/2 sacks of Stroud.

Stroud was 16-of-27 for 167 yards and a touchdown. David Montgomery had 11 carries for 33 yards, and Xavier Hutchinson caught three passes for 51 yards.

Texans defensive end Will Anderson had 2.5 sacks of Jones.

title: Giants manager Tony Vitello ends rough first season with MLB-high seventh ejection
description: The Giants took a big step backward in their first year under the former college coach.
fullText:
Tony Vitello's first season as an MLB manager ended a few innings earlier than expected.

The San Francisco Giants manager was ejected in the third inning of his team's season finale against the Los Angeles Dodgers on Sunday, responding irately to a check-swing call from first-base umpire Marvin Hudson. Hudson gave Vitello a quick boot, prompting Vitello to get his money's worth.

It was Vitello's seventh ejection this season, the most by any manager in MLB and the most by an National League manager since then-Cincinnati Reds manager David Bell's seven in 2023.

Tony Vitello has been ejected after arguing this check-swing call 🤬 pic.twitter.com/XcobZmbhA3

Vitello and the Giants did appear to have a point. With a 2-2 count, one out and runners on first and second, Dodgers star Mookie Betts' bat clearly went past the plate on a high fastball from Sam Hentges. It should have been strike 3, which Hentges got one pitch later on a swinging strike on another high fastball.

Check swing calls are explicitly a judgement call for umpires and are not reviewable. They are also a bit of a sore spot for the Giants in games against the Dodgers, as a 107-win Giants team had its season ended in the 2021 NLDS against the Dodgers when the umpires ruled Wilmer Flores swung at a pitch.

Vitello wasn't the manager for that game. He joined the Giants last offseason as one of MLB's most outside-the-box managerial hires in recent memory. Before 2026, Vitello had never worked in professional baseball, not even as a minor-league player. Giants president of baseball operations Buster Posey made the hire after Vitello's successful tenure as head coach at Tennessee, with the Volunteers winning the College World Series in 2024.

The Giants tasked Vitello with steering a veteran roster looking to make the playoffs for the first time since that 2021 checked-swing call. Instead, they took a massive step backwards, with the club going from an 81-81 record in 2025 under veteran MLB manager Bob Melvin to a 65-96 record under Vitello entering Sunday. They would be in last place in any other division save the historically awful AL West.

That under-performance isn't entirely Vitello's fault. An aged roster was beset by injuries, with Rafael Devers, Willy Adames, Matt Chapman, Jung Hoo Lee, Harrison Bader, Logan Webb and many more on the injured list as of Sunday, to say nothing of certain players' underperformance.

That said, Vitello also didn't exactly impress observers. The team got off to a bad start with a number of clubhouse incidents and never recovered. Vitello also caught significant flack for his handling, or lack thereof, of the Giants' Pride Night incident in June.

Vitello was a risky bet for Posey, whose own tenure hasn't been sparkling since he replaced Farhan Zaidi in 2024, which was a significant philosophical shift for the Giants. It's enough for Vitello to be considered on the hot seat for 2027, if he isn't there already.

title: The RUNDOWN: Everything you need to know about the Bears in Week 3 against the Eagles
description: LAKE FOREST, Ill. — Bears offensive coordinator Press Taylor is just one month older than quarterback Case Keenum. So he has a deep appreciation and respect for what the veteran...
fullText:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. — Bears offensive coordinator Press Taylor is just one month older than quarterback Case Keenum.

So he has a deep appreciation and respect for what the veteran did this past week to prepare for the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football.

"I just haven't practiced in 15 years and I don't know that I could get up and do that every single day," Taylor said.

With that said, here's everything you need to know from the podium to the injury report to the Bears locker room before kickoff in Week 3.

Tyson Bagent officially cleared concussion protocol on Sunday. Case Keenum got the majority of the practice work this past week but it's always possible that Bagent plays.

"Since it's progressed along, he was able to be in meetings (Friday) and now he's in practice (Saturday), and so he's right on track to be right where he needs to be," Ben Johnson said on Saturday. "And I think mentally he's going to be in a good spot for what we're asking to do."

Johnson has talked too much about the significance of practice reps for all players in the past to overlook how important they were for Keenum over the past few days. But Bagent also had good moments against the Minnesota Vikings that he can build upon.

"I thought he did a great job giving us an opportunity at the end of the game," offensive coordinator Press Taylor said. "You are facing that (Vikings) defense. It's a tough situation. He gave us an opportunity to get down there. Obviously, it goes without being said, we'd like to have maximized both those possessions that end up inside the 12-yard line better than we did. But I thought in terms of being a backup thrown into a tough situation, he did a great job giving us an opportunity."

Caleb Williams was ruled out for Monday night but his status remains something to watch throughout Monday. ESPN/NFL Network reported that Williams is dealing with a Grade 2 hamstring pull and could miss three or four weeks.

My understanding from the start was that Williams was always looking at a multi-week absence. Playing against the Eagles was never a realistic option. The question was how quickly Williams would start to recover and progress.

As my colleague Adam Hoge pointed out on X on Sunday, the clearest indicator of the severity of Williams' injury will come at 3 p.m. on Monday – the deadline for roster moves before kickoff.

Placing Williams on injured reserve would guarantee a four-week absence but also provide the Bears with an available roster spot – which they could use with linebacker Noah Sewell and defensive lineman Shemar Turner nearing their activations from the PUP list.

Here's one thing for certain: the long-term health of Williams will be prioritized. The Bears will not rush him back. The organization can still hope for the best with Williams but it also has planned for the worst. The Bears can turn to Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum.

It might be different if Keenum was just added to the roster with Caleb Williams (QB1) and Tyson Bagent (QB2) ailing. But Keenum has played an integral role behind the scenes since joining the Bears in April 2025.

"It's always fun, kind of get to work with a vet," tight end Cole Kmet said. "Obviously, they've seen so much and done so much, and how many times has he set a play call in the huddle? So it's cool to kind of get that vibe from him. And I know he's super excited about the opportunity, all that type of stuff."

Keenum took the first-team reps during the Bears' prep for the Eagles.

"The way he commands everything, he's been doing it for a long time," running back D'Andre Swift said. "So he's been great."

Keenum is part of the Bears' investment in Williams but also the position overall.

"(It's) just his professionalism," offensive coordinator Press Taylor said. "He's obviously done it a really long time and at a high level, and he's been through kind of every role you can be in in a quarterback room, from undrafted to a franchise guy to a backup to an up-and-down starter. And so I think all those lessons have really kind of molded him into the quarterback he is today. He's probably not the same quarterback he was 12, 13 years ago, five years ago.

"And then … he's been with us since Day 1, so he's watched this thing get built, he's had input on the way we've done things. And now it's really cool to see him get a little bit more opportunity here in practice and see how he handles it. If his opportunity comes, I don't think anybody has any doubt he'll be ready for the moment."

He didn't practice Wednesday, Thursday (estimation) or Friday because of soreness in his hip. But he was back in action on Saturday.

Santos doesn't have an injury designation for Monday night.

"I just felt some soreness after the (Vikings) game," Santos told reporters. "I felt good that it wasn't an injury-related thing and I'm thankful for coach Johnson and (special teams coordinator Richard Hightower) for letting me rest. I don't think I've ever had a rest day. But maybe it's that point in my career that after a rainy game, kicking a lot of wet balls, they're heavier. I felt like my body just felt a little sore. I just rested and then felt good (Saturday)."

It's because he's "Miami tough," according to Ben Johnson.

"I was fortunate to be down there for seven years, and so I do think there's something in the water down there," Johnson said. "Guys are a little bit different in terms of how they're brought up. And so it's good. I said it at the end of training camp, we have a roster full of guys that are fighting – fighting to be on that grass and be on the field and help their teammates win."

Stevenson was initially deemed week-to-week with a hamstring injury, which he suffered against the Vikings. But he returned to practice on Friday and now he doesn't have an injury designation for Week 3.

It's been an injury-filled few weeks for Stevenson. He got banged up in training camp at Halas Hall and later during the joint practice against the Tennessee Titans. Stevenson was later evaluated twice for a concussion in Week 1 against the Carolina Panthers, the second time because of a stinger.

Last year was last year regardless of the 281 rushing yards produced by the Bears in Philadelphia.

Last week, Swift felt like he left yards – and definitely a touchdown because of his fumble – on the field against the Vikings.

"I feel like I missed a couple out there, but (it's) a different style of defense that was kind of getting thrown at us," Swift said. "Another opportunity to make it right (on Monday)."

Week 3 is Week 3 regardless of opponent.

"(We) just so happen to play the Eagles," Swift said.

Mannion is in his first year as the Eagles' offensive coordinator. He's a first-time playcaller. He spent the past two years with the Green Bay Packers as an offensive assistant and then quarterbacks coach.

A former quarterback, Mannion is also not far removed from his own playing career. His last stint came in December 2023 on the Seattle Seahawks' practice squad.

Allen's first season as a defensive coordinator came in 2011 with the Denver Broncos.

"We're obviously defending the scheme and as we're going through this, we're trying to evaluate, 'OK, what is Philly as it's been for the last few years? What are the new wrinkles that Sean's bringing over with him?' And (it's) just trying to see how they're going to attack the game," Allen said. "But we've really got to defend the plays and the formations that are set before us. My job will be to try to get a feel for what their plan is and how they're trying to attack us and then we've got to be able to adjust to whatever that might be."

Bears vs. Eagles Predictions: What's left in the tank for QB Case Keenum?

From Week 1 to Week 2, Roush's snaps on offense increased from 12 to 20 but dropped from 28 to nine on special teams.

Roush wasn't set on first-and-10 on the Minnesota Vikings' 30 when tight end Colston Loveland had a 14-yard catch. His illegal shift wiped out the gain. It also was the start of four penalties in five plays for the Bears.

Roush also had a drop in the red zone four plays before Caleb Williams suffered his hamstring injury.

On special teams, it first appeared that Roush was to blame for the blocked field goal by the Vikings. But a closer look revealed that the snap count was off. Veteran long snapper Scott Daly later replaced rookie Beau Gardner on the roster.

But will Roush's playing time come next?

"It's not the only phase he played on, and he graded out extremely well on kickoff return. He graded out extremely well on punt," special teams coordinator Richard Hightower said. "So he's got to keep growing him. He's not on punt return yet or on kickoff last game. He was the first game. He did an outstanding job on kickoff the first game. So he's a young player that we're developing. He cares. He's working his tail off, and we'll continue to develop him. So that's not the only thing he does. We all got to be better, alright. So I'm not going to single out, Sam. We all got to be better."

The team won't give up on developing rookie Beau Gardner.

But some stability was needed after the miscues in Week 3.

"He's a good friend," kicker Cairo Santos told reporters. "We stayed in touch, even trying to get him back here in free agency and helping him get other opportunities out there. It just felt like riding a bike when he came out there and executing our kicks (Saturday) and just kind of getting that rhythm again."

And it won't include Ozzy Trapilo quite yet despite his own progress.

The idea behind it is to keep Braxton Jones fresh for late in games. Backup Theo Benedet has played 38 snaps in two weeks.

"We'll see how the game goes," offensive coordinator Press Taylor said. "We've kind of got a plan going into every single week. We'll discuss it as a staff early in the week, kind of see how it shakes out, and then we'll stamp it somewhere along the week and going into the game. We'll determine whatever gives us the best opportunity to win.

In two games, he has just one catch for three yards on five targets.

"I think obviously we want the ball," Loveland said after practice on Wednesday. "Everyone in here wants the ball. We're here for a reason and we want to make plays and help our team win. But there's other ways to make plays on the ground in the run game. I'm just doing what I'm asked, and like we were talking about, there's going to be opportunities, so I just gotta take full advantage when it arises."

That said, it's time to just throw the film of Week 2 out and focus on the Eagles.

"I don't think it's realistic to think anybody's going to air the ball out the way it went last week in the pouring rain," offensive coordinator Press Taylor said.

title: Allen, Bills outlast Chargers 24-16 despite committing 5 turnovers
description: Josh Allen scored two touchdowns rushing and the Buffalo Bills overcame a five-turnover outing to pull out a 24-16 victory over the winless Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday.  Allen’s second score, a 1-yard plunge with 7:35 left, gave Buffalo its first lead.  The Bills then sealed the win on James Cook’s 3-yard run four minutes later, and after Buffalo’s defense forced Justin Herbert's incompletion on fourth down at the Chargers 45.
fullText:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. (AP) — Josh Allen scored two touchdowns rushing and the Buffalo Bills overcame a five-turnover outing to pull out a 24-16 victory over the winless Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday.

Allen's second score, a 1-yard plunge with 7:35 left, gave Buffalo its first lead. The Bills then sealed the win on James Cook's 3-yard run four minutes later, and after Buffalo's defense forced Justin Herbert's incompletion on fourth down at the Chargers 45.

Buffalo improved to 3-0 despite Allen's two interceptions and lost fumble. Cook and tight end Dalton Kincaid also lost fumbles.

The problem for the Chargers was their inability to take advantage — with three of Buffalo's turnovers occurring in Bills' territory.

Los Angeles opened the scoring on Herbert's 1-yard shovel pass to Keaton Mitchell on a drive set up after Cook lost a fumble on Buffalo's first snap from scrimmage. And the Chargers built a 10-0 first-quarter lead on Cameron Dicker's 31-yard field goal that followed Allen's first interception.

For much of the remainder of the game, the Chargers resembled the sputtering offense that opened the season being limited to 14 points per outing and combining for more punts (seven) and turnovers (five) than touchdowns (four) in its first two games.

The 0-3 start is L.A.'s worst since opening the 2017 season with three consecutive losses.

Buffalo, meantime, is 3-0 through three outings for the third straight year and fifth time in nine seasons under Allen.

Allen's two touchdown runs upped his career total from scrimmage to 87 (85 rushing and two receiving) — tying Hall of Famers Thurman Thomas and Andre Reed for the team record.

Chargers: at the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday.

Bills: Close three-game homestand by hosting the New England Patriots on Sunday.

title: 1 baffling Drake Maye stat is either terrible or incredible news for Patriots QB
description: Doing something only Drew Brees AND Rex Grossman have only done the last two decades is, uh, something.
fullText:
The malaise that haunted Drake Maye through last winter has chased him into the 2026 regular season. The New England Patriots quarterback hasn't just been bogged down by pressure, he's also been the league's most careless player with the ball in his hands. Through three games he's turned the ball over seven times.

As a result, the defending AFC champions are 1-2 following a rout at the hands of the Jacksonville Jaguars Sunday afternoon. New England was briefly competitive before reckless throws and horrible decisions derailed what was one of the league's most efficient offenses just a year ago. Maye's offense mustered only six points. He was replaced in favor of backup Tommy DeVito late in the fourth quarter, effectively waving a white flag on the team's eventual 35-6 loss.

There's a very dim silver lining for last year's regular season MVP runner-up. There's a 50/50 shot it ends with a Super Bowl ring and Hall of Fame ceremony!

There aren't too many situations in which you get Rex Grossman and Drew Brees compared in the same sentence. Maye's awful play has united the unlikely bedfellows. Unfortunately, between his start to the season and his playoff debut last winter, the Patriots' quarterback is trending toward Grossman rather than the New Orleans Saints legend.
